content.comment_body: Hi everyone, I have more than 30 [company_name] [product_name] at different sites performing identical tasks. Each unit is connected to a [product_name], with IP addresses set to 192.168.0.200 for the controller and 192.168.0.201. On one unit, the IP address is lost after several days, requiring the user to reset the addresses for both devices to restore operation. Since both devices are affected, I don't believe the issue is with the controller itself. Has anyone encountered this before or know what could be causing it? Thank you for your assistance.

I haven't come across any cases where a [product_name] or [product_name] 'forgets' its IP settings. These addresses are saved in flash memory and should remain unchanged, even after power loss. If I were you, I would consider submitting a support request.

Hello [user_name], 1. Since all devices perform the same function, try swapping the problematic unit with another to test if the issue persists with the device or its network connections. 2. In my experience, sometimes operational mistakes can cause unexpected problems. Have you considered whether human error might be a factor?

analysis.insight_summary: Community members reported that [company_name] [product_name] with attached [product_name] occasionally lose manually set IP configurations, leading to networking disruptions. Both devices need their IPs reset to resume communication. The behavior seems unusual since IP settings should persist in flash memory, even through power cycles. Other users suggest procedural mistakes or physical interventions might contribute to the issue, as they have not observed similar cases before.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect IP configuration on both devices to persist reliably without needing repeated manual setup. They want consistent network operation in line with device specifications and memory retention as described in the documentation.
